entities.summary:
Jaime Cardona (Jaime Francesc Folc de Cardona i de Gandia) was a prominent Catholic cardinal who played a crucial role in the Catholic Church during the late 15th century. He was a key figure in the Catholic Reformation and was instrumental in shaping the Church's policies and practices. Born into a noble family in the Principality of Catalonia, Cardona rose to prominence through his education and theological expertise, eventually becoming a cardinal in 1461. He was chosen by Pope Pius II to oversee the reform of the Church's practices and was a key advisor to the Pope. Cardona's influence extended beyond the Church, as he played a role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of the region. His legacy continues to be felt today, with many of his theological writings remaining relevant to this day. One of his most notable contributions was his role in the Council of Florence, where he helped to shape the Church's stance on the Filioque clause. Despite his significant influence, Cardona's life was cut short when he died on December 10, 1466, at the age of 46. His death was a significant loss to the Church, and his legacy has been remembered and honored by scholars and historians for centuries.


Cardona's significance can be seen in several key areas, including his role in the Catholic Reformation, his influence on the Church's policies and practices, and his contributions to theological writings. His legacy has had a lasting impact on the Church and continues to be felt today.

Cardona's causes included his noble birth, his education and theological expertise, and his appointment as cardinal. These factors combined to shape his career and influence his decisions. The Church's policies and practices were also a significant cause for Cardona, as he played a key role in shaping the Church's stance on several important issues.
